Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border payments appear to rely on banks’ SWIFT access via the BCSTP (SWIFT Alliance) rather than regional instant payment links; UNCDF notes banks access international SWIFT via BCSTP and discusses need/recommendations for regional links (e.g., PAPSS/REPPS) but does not describe an implemented cross-border instant payment linkage ([UNCDF Payment Infrastructure Assessment](https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-SaoTome-April2025.pdf)).

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: São Tomé and Príncipe has a general personal data protection law: Law No. 03/2016 on Protection of Personal Data, establishing ANPDP and regulating processing/transfer of personal data; no evidence found of payment-specific data provisions ([Data Protection Africa fact sheet](https://dataprotection.africa/sao-tome-and-principe/);[Law Gratis overview](https://www.lawgratis.com/blog-detail/cyber-law-at-sao-tome-and-principe-1)).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: UNCDF’s April 2025 assessment describes an operational national retail payment infrastructure (the Dobra24 interbank ATM/POS network, operating since Oct 2011) alongside modernization work (PISPIF) to implement a national switch/disaster recovery and later an RTGS (SPGTR) via an Automatic Transfer System, indicating the system exists but is still being upgraded rather than a fully modern nationwide instant payment system ([UNCDF Payment Infrastructure Assessment](https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-SaoTome-April2025.pdf)). AfDB announced a 2023 loan to upgrade the National Switch with RTGS/ACH functionalities, reinforcing that infrastructure is being enhanced/expanded ([AfDB press release](https://afdb.africa-newsroom.com/press/sao-tome-and-principe-african-development-bank-signs-32-million-loan-agreement-for-upgrade-of-national-switch-payment-system?lang=en)).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: UNCDF reports very low DFS usage and cites BCSTP NFIS demand-side survey (2017) with only ~24% financial inclusion and low usage of electronic channels (ATM/debit card/internet banking = 23% of transaction volume; bank transfers via DFS = 3%; business payments via digital = 1%), implying active digital payment users are likely <20% ([UNCDF Payment Infrastructure Assessment](https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-SaoTome-April2025.pdf)).
